newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BIRMINGHAM MULL NAME CHANGE TO RAISE MONEY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BIRMINGHAM MULL NAME CHANGE TO RAISE MONEY.

text.p: The managing director of Birmingham City said on Monday she would be willing to change the English club's name to attract sponsorship.
"I would be prepared to change the name of the club and I think that is the way most clubs are going," the first division club's Karren Brady told BBC television.
Birmingham are determined to return to the top flight of English soccer for the first time since the 1980s.
The club pulled out of a proposed 1.8 million pound ($3 million) signing of Norwegian striker Martin Aarst on Monday, with money an issue although not the main one.
"After weighing everything up, including the transfer fee and the player's wages, I've decided not to pursue his signature," manager Trevor Francis said.
Brady said a name change could put the club on a stronger financial footing.
"We would change the name, either of St Andrews or Birmingham City," she said.
"That would be something which is going to happen with such partnerships in future -- and I hope it happens."
Birmingham City have changed their name several times in the past, with the most recent mutation coming in 1945 when they added the City to what had been just Birmingham.

No clubs in top-level English soccer carry sponsors' names, although some stadiums do, and the League of Wales runners-up are Inter Cable Tel Cardiff. They play Celtic of Scotland in a UEFA Cup qualifier in Cardiff on Wednesday.
A Football Association spokesman said any change of name would need the F.A.'s approval and added that there were strict rules governing visible sponsorship.
"When we get a firm proposal, we'll take a look at it," the spokesman added.
A League spokeswoman said that one concern would be that clubs would change their name every time they got a new sponsor, throwing the sport into confusion.
